newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-DEFEAT GIVES ELS NEW PERSPECTIVE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DEFEAT GIVES ELS NEW PERSPECTIVE.

text.p: A year ago Ernie Els almost had the British Open in his grip -- and then let it slip through his fingers.
That experience, he says, has changed him.
"To come through an experience like that, it changes your mindset, and hopefully I've grown up a lot since then," he said on Wednesday. "I am a lot different this year."
At Royal Lytham and St Annes last year, the tall South African began the final round eight behind leader Tom Lehman and did not give himself much of a chance.

"After nine holes I was two under and no-one else was doing much. Then I made four birdies in five holes and I think I was even in the lead at one stage. Then I made some mental errors coming in," Els recalled.

"I was thinking more of putting the ball just in play instead of really going out and trying to birdie the last three holes. Maybe I didn't have the confidence I have right now, and that's obviously why I made those mistakes."
Those mistakes cost him two bogeys in the last three holes and allowed Lehman to take the trophy despite a two-over-par 73 final round. Els had to settle for a second place tie.
"It really took me a while to get over it. I didn't play well for about two or three months and my game really went away a little bit," Els said.
"But experience comes with a couple of disappointments. I think this year I'm ready."
With his recent record, Els has every reason to feel confident. He won last month's U.S. Open for the second time, vanquishing Lehman, among others, with a magnificent final round.
The following week Els went on to win the Buick Open and rewarded himself with a two-week holiday with his family.
He returned to golf last week at Loch Lomond in the World Invitational and took second place -- with Lehman winning to show he is also in top form in readiness for his British Open title defence.
"In this game there is a very fine line between victory and defeat," Els said. "You've just got to try to be as positive as you can and play the shot that you are comfortable with.
